title.narrative: COVID-19: Responsive COVID-19 Vaccination for Recovery Project under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility

description.narrative:
The project will provide Maldives with needed financing to sustain and upgrade its national coronavirus disease (COVID-19) vaccination program, within its overall expanded program of immunization (EPI), through the project investment component (PIC) modality of the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility (APVAX) of the Asian Development Bank (ADB). The PIC grant will support investments for the storage, distribution, delivery, and administration of COVID-19 vaccines, along with related investments in capacity building, which will help ensure the success of the government's COVID-19 vaccine booster program.
The project is aligned with five of the operational priorities of ADB's Strategy 2030: (i) addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities; (ii) accelerating progress in gender equality; (iii) tackling climate change, building climate and disaster resilience, and enhancing environmental sustainability; (iv) strengthening governance and institutional capacity; and (v) fostering regional cooperation and integration. It is consistent with ADB's country partnership strategy, 2020-2024 for Maldives, which prioritizes the strengthening of Maldives' health system.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity of vaccine storage and transport system increased Indicator: By 2025, at least 7 sea vehicles made operational for 6 atolls and the Greater Malé region. Progress/Status: Contract extension has been signed as extension approval received from MOH Bid committee and ADB. New contract end date is 15th Jan 2026.
Sea Trials held on 13th and 14th of October 2025. Some changes to both 40- and 45-feet boats were suggested by the naval architect.
The first shipment of 2 speed boats of 40ft will depart to Maldives on 1st of January 2026.
All seven speedboats were delivered to the Maldives by 22 February 2026. Inspections were subsequently conducted by the Naval Architect Consultant, and all vessels were successfully cleared on 12 March 2026. Following clearance, all speedboats were delivered to their respective designated health facilities Data Source: PMU records and EPI reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity of vaccine storage and transport system increased Indicator: By 2027, at least 1 refrigerated trucks and 1 van operational in the Greater Malé region. Progress/Status: Advance payment and performance guarantee claim approved and paid by Dhivehi Insurance on 16 December 2025
PMU requested from the relevant department of MOH to confirm the payment.
Only one bid was received in the 4th round of procurement, and the bidder failed to comply with the technical specifications provided.
PMU will be discussing with the relevant teams to decide whether to proceed with the 5th round of procurement.
With regards to the refrigerated truck, PMU has received technical specifications. PMU is working on bidding documents.
For the supply of 1 van, a contract was signed with the supplier on 30 May 2024. However, due to a delay in making the advance payment, a contract amendment was made stipulating that the delivery date shall be counted from the date of advance payment date. Similarly, due to the delay in advance payment date the proposed model of the van was not available and change in model of the van was requested from the supplier. As per the PFR policy direction was required along with the bid committee approval which was received on 19th December. Informed the supplier to proceed with the revised recent model of the van without any price change. Awaiting for the delivery. The recent mission found that the supplier did not deliver or extend the performance bond, and the contract has expired. The mission instructed to get ADB approval for rebidding. As a result, the procurement plan was revised.
ADB team recommended changing the procurement method from Open Competitive Bidding (OCB) to Bidding (OCB) to Request for Quotation (RFQ), and the PMU is currently proceeding with the required actions.
The latest update is that the EA/MOF has decided not to proceed with the procurement of the van and truck due to cost overruns in the civil works contract, where the evaluated bid price significantly exceeded the engineer's estimate. As a result, the Government has opted to reallocate the available funds to support the building construction component, which is considered a higher priority at this stage. Data Source: PMU records and EPI reports Actual value:

Output: Human resource capacity of the Expanded Program on Immunization enhanced. Indicator: By 2024, at least 50% of hired contract staff (supporting central EPI program, national health data center, and MOH's biomedical services unit) are women Achievement: 50 Progress/Status: Out of 8 target positions, 8 has been filled which is 100% of the target staffs (50% women and 50% men). Data Source: Participant's feedback survey

Output: Indicator Indicator: By 2025, at least 257 tablets for vaccination data entry deployed to all public health units and government hospitals across the country Achievement: 257 Progress/Status: As per the contract, the tablets were delivered during Q4 2023, and their deployment commenced during Q4 2023.
As of Q2 2024, all the tablets have been distributed to public health units in atolls for EPI data entry purpose as per the relevant department of MOH.
This indicator has been completed.
Data Source: EPI reports and PMU records

Output: Information management of the Expanded Program on Immunization strengthened for COVID-19 vaccination and routine immunization Indicator: By 2025, at least 75% of the EPI delivery staff (70% of them women) with increased skills in key vaccination-related technical areas Progress/Status: PMU plans to conduct the training short-term training program on Cold Chain Repair and Maintenance in June 2026.
During the reporting period, the PMU communicated with the Maldives Polytechnic and is currently working to finalize the program details. In addition, the list of participants for the training program has been received by the PMU.
Under the long-term scholarship program, the agreement has been signed with the seventh awardee. Currently, four candidates have completed their studies, while three are continuing. The PMU is coordinating with the relevant departments of the Ministry of Health to facilitate their recruitment in line with the Civil Service bond agreement.
Data Source: PMU records Actual value:

Output: Capacity of vaccine storage and transport system increased Indicator: By 2027, a new central vaccine storage building with GESI-responsive and climate resilient features and additional 30 cubic meters of storage capacity constructed. Progress/Status: The payment for the detailed design approval to Housing Development Corporation has been fully settled. Following this, HDC officially handed over the land to the Ministry of Health on 17 February 2026 and completed the demarcation of the plot.
The contract with Design Link Associates Pvt Ltd was signed on 23 September 2024. The inception mission happened in the last week of October 2024. The detailed design is complete and approved. The draft bidding documents were sent for ADB approval on 24 July 2025. The latest loan review mission took place from 15 to 19 June 2025, during which the procurement plan and CAD projections were reviewed and updated with new timelines. The loan was extended until 30 June 2028. Upon ADB NOL, the contract was awarded on 19 July 2026. The contractor needs to sign the contract and start work. Data Source: PMU records and EPI reports Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: By 2027, a health data center and a back-up data center established Progress/Status: The items needed to establish a health data center and a backup data center have been awarded and delivered to the Ministry of Health.
According to the relevant department/division within the MoH back-up data center established. Hence this indicator has been completed.
Data Source: Health IT department data and EPI reports Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: Indicator Indicator: Vaccination data disaggregated by sex, age, location, comorbidity conditions, and nationality compiled and made available in the systems. Progress/Status: The national vaccine information systems (DHIS-2 and COVID-19 vaccination information system DHIFAAU registers real-time sex- and age- disaggregated data on persons receiving vaccines from EPI and COVID-19 vaccination program. Reports are generated regularly by MOH relevant department/division.
As of Q4 2025, Total % of Routine immunization coverage was at 100.11%, out of which 49.67% male and 53.45% female.
As reported in the previous QPR, the COVID-19 situation in the Maldives remained under control, and the government opt not to mandate COVID-19 vaccinations. Further details can be found in the attached annex 8.
Data Source: EPI reports Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2025 Target value: Y
The deployment of COVID-19 vaccines and other vaccines under the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) effectively managed

By 2027, the average transport cost to MOH per dose of COVID-19 and routine immunization vaccines from Malé to atolls reduced by 25%. Progress/Status: PMU (with ADB consultant) finalized the revised methodology to calculate the vaccine transportation cost.
• PMU gathered information for the year 2019 (the year before COVID-19), • Estimated total cost for sending vaccines to the Atolls: USD 65479 • Total number of vaccine doses sent to each Atoll: 262,030 doses distributed in 2019 • PMU utilized this information to calculate the existing cost incurred for vaccine transportation • According to the forecast, with the introduction of speed boats to deliver the vaccines to atolls, there will be a cost reduction of 60% to the government Data Source: EPI reports Actual value:

By 2027, routine immunization coverage by age and sex are maintained at more than 95% of eligible populations. Progress/Status: The Routine Immunization Coverage report is done as an annual compilation, and the data compilation process is still ongoing. Consequently, the sex and age disaggregated data for routine immunization coverage is currently unavailable.
As per the relevant department MOH plans to generate the data through DHIS2 system once all health facilities update their records by Q4 2024. Immunization coverage by age and sex can be obtained once the records are fully updated from all health facilities. Data Source: EPI reports Actual value:

By 2027, routine immunization and COVID-19 sex-disaggregated vaccination data reported annually. Progress/Status: The coverage for COVID-19 vaccination by sex ratio for Q4 2023 were maintained by the Health Protection Agency.
% of COVID-19 Vaccination coverage for Q4 2023 was: *Female 47.37% *Male 52.63%
Total % of Routine immunization coverage was at 99% as of Q3 2023 (Calculated from the annual routine immunization coverage report by Health Protection Agency)
As per Health Protection Agency, currently the Routine immunization coverage reports are being prepared on an annual basis.
